P1.reason: A lumps almost the whole game into one blob; B separates movement, board geometry, state update and initial setup, and game end/goals, much closer to rules a player names.

differences.reason: Hurts: one giant group merges movement, capture, setup, termination and scoring into nothing a player would name.
Mixed: initial setup with board update is coherent-ish, but setup and state update are distinct rules.
Helps: game end and winning conditions grouped together; stray capture rule slightly muddies it.
Helps: forward direction with straight/diagonal moves captures pawn movement, though capture overlaps.
Helps: adjacency drives diagonal moves and captures, a recognisable diagonal rule.
Helps somewhat: board coordinates and occupancy form the board definition.
Helps: legal moves, move application and noop form the turn/move-making rule.
